results.name: Time-of-day probe of the shipped model (SM76): does a card’s predicted R change with the hour its review is planned?
results.eval: 6 held-out users, 1,800 sampled reviews (elapsed ≥ 1 day); big model (fork RWKV) as shipped in the fork
results.fork: Spread of predicted R over the same review moved −8 h to +8 h on the same day, in R points
results.takeaway: Small for intervals, a little noise in displayed R: the forgetting curve that sets intervals moves 0.17 points (median) over ±8 h, and only for 1–3 day cards (1.0 point), where 8 hours is real forgetting. The displayed R (query row) moves about 0.5 points (median, p90 2 points) from the elapsed-time sin/cos phase alone, with no average direction, including on cards due in over 100 days

detail.verdict: No action needed for scheduling; the displayed-R wobble is a clock-phase artefact worth knowing about, not fixing now
notes: Each sampled review is re-asked with the review time moved by −8, −6, …, +8 hours on the same Anki day; day number, interval in days and the day’s review counts stay the same; spread = max − min over the 9 times, in R points
Curve R: the card’s stored curve read at elapsed time + shift (what the fork uses for intervals); it falls on average 0.28 points at +8 h earlier…0.12 later, i.e. ordinary forgetting
Phase only: just the daily sin/cos of elapsed seconds is shifted; its mean change is ~0 at every shift (−0.03 to 0.00 points), so it is jitter, not a time-of-day bias

results.name: Time of day and weekday check (SM75): does the clock carry recall information the model does not use?
results.eval: 599 training users, 39.4M labelled reviews; big model (1 leak-free epoch) per-review predictions
results.fork: LogLoss change from a correction by clock bin; negative = better
results.takeaway: No useful signal: raw recall does vary with the hour (about 86.5% at 5–7 am vs 83% in the afternoon and evening), but the model already predicts that variation from what is reviewed when. A correction by hour, weekday or hours since the day’s first review changes LogLoss by at most 0.02%, about 30 times smaller than the small model’s remaining gap to the big model

detail.verdict: Not worth a model input: the clock adds almost nothing beyond the inputs the model already has
